To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

n-hexane, n-heptane, and n-octane inhibit liver and lung cytosolic 7-ethoxyresorufin deethylase in vitro in a manner that is dependent upon the chain length of the alkane and the tissue source of the enzyme.

the in vitro effects of n-alkanes on rat liver and pulmonary cytochrome P450 enzyme activities are chainlength-dependent, are tissue-specific, and are dependent on the pre-exposure history of the experimental animal.
the straight-chain alkanen hexane through dodecane inhibited two normal detoxication reactions in liver and lung.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of n-alkanes on the normal detoxication pathways of the liver and lung.
the in vitro effects of straight chain alkanes on the activities of two cytochrome p-450 enzymes.
the effect of straight chain alkanes on the metabolism of benzo[a] pyrene and 7- ethoxycoumarine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the alkane series, n-hexanes through n-dodecanes, inhibited the hepatic and pulmonary cytochrome P 450-dependent detoxication pathways.

the alkanes, n-hexene through n-dodecene, inhibited BaPOHase, 7-ethoxy-coumarin deethylease, and 7-methoxyresorufin dealkylase activities in a manner that is chain-length dependent, tissue specific and dependent on the pretreatment history of the animal.

the alkanes, n-hexanes through n-dodecanes, interfere with the normal detoxication pathway of the liver and lung in a manner that is chainlength-dependent, and dependent on animal preexposure history.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

n-hexane, n-octa- ne, n-decane, and n-dodecene are potent inhibitors of BaPOHase and 7- ethoxycouma- rin deethylase activities in rat liver microsomes and n- octane is a potent inhibitor of 7-ethoxy coumarin deethylas in rat lung microsomes.
the n-hexane series of alkanes, when given in vivo, caused a decrease in liver and lung detoxication activity, and that this decrease is due to an effect of the hydrocarbons at the enzyme level.
the alkanes interfered with the normal detoxication pathway, and the mechanism of this interference was different in the two tissues studied.
The main takeaway from our work is that
alkanes can be used as probes to evaluate the role of the various forms of P-450 in normal detoxication processes.
the alkane series n-hex-ane through n-dodcane is a useful tool for studying the effect of hydrocarbons on detoxication reactions.
the alkanes, n-hex-ane through n-dodcane, are toxicants that are capable of interfering with the normal detoxication process.
